proposed.explanation: Japanese cherry trees do not thrive in coastal salt spray; exotic species require more maintenance and may fail. Mango and calamansi can work, but vegetables are temporary and not suitable for long-term landscaping structure. Monoculture creates pest vulnerability and biodiversity loss; diversity is essential. Narra is a native, salt-tolerant Philippine tree. Fire tree thrives in tropical conditions. Pili is native and produces crops. Native salt-tolerant groundcovers (such as Philippine sedge or vetiver) survive coastal exposure. These species reduce irrigation needs, resist local pests, and provide ecological value. Select native species adapted to local climate, soil, and hazards (salt spray, flooding). Native plants thrive with minimal input, reducing lifecycle costs and environmental impact.
